title: OSHA general industry walking-working surfaces practice questions
description: Free OSHA general industry walking-working surfaces practice questions on 29 CFR 1910 Subpart D. Every answer is explained and linked to its section.

questions.question: Under 1910.22(d)(2), what must happen when a hazardous condition on a walking-working surface cannot be corrected or repaired immediately?

options.A: Employees may keep using the surface for up to 7 days
options.B: The hazard is guarded to prevent employees from using the surface until it is corrected or repaired
options.C: A note in the maintenance log is enough until the next scheduled repair
options.D: Employees may use the surface once they have been told about the hazard

questions.explanation: Hazardous conditions must be corrected or repaired before the surface is used again, and "if the correction or repair cannot be made immediately, the hazard must be guarded to prevent employees from using the walking-working surface until the hazard is corrected or repaired."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.22, General requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under 1910.22(b), what load must the employer ensure each walking-working surface can support?

options.A: Twice the heaviest load placed on it during the past year
options.B: A uniform 50 pounds per square foot, whatever the surface is used for
options.C: Only the weight of the employees who walk on it, not their tools or materials
options.D: The maximum intended load for that surface

questions.explanation: Under the loads paragraph, "the employer must ensure that each walking-working surface can support the maximum intended load for that surface."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.22, General requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under 1910.22(a)(2), what must be maintained when wet processes are used in a workroom?

options.A: Drainage
options.B: A written spill log reviewed once a year
options.C: Standing water no deeper than 1 inch
options.D: A closed door between the workroom and other areas

questions.explanation: "When wet processes are used, drainage must be maintained" and, to the extent feasible, dry standing places such as false floors, platforms, and mats must be provided.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.22, General requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under 1910.23(b)(3), how far apart must the steps on a stepstool be spaced, measured between the centerlines of the steps?

options.A: Not less than 6 inches and not more than 10 inches
options.B: Not less than 12 inches and not more than 16 inches
options.C: Not less than 8 inches and not more than 12 inches
options.D: Not less than 14 inches and not more than 18 inches

questions.explanation: The rule says "Steps on stepstools are spaced not less than 8 inches (20 cm) apart and not more than 12 inches (30 cm) apart, as measured between the centerlines of the steps."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.23, Ladders (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: What does 1910.23(b)(5) require for wooden ladders?

options.A: They are replaced every 5 years, whatever their condition
options.B: They are painted a high-visibility color so defects stand out
options.C: They are not coated with any material that may obscure structural defects
options.D: They are used only by employees trained as carpenters

questions.explanation: The employer must ensure "Wooden ladders are not coated with any material that may obscure structural defects." A coating such as opaque paint could hide cracks or other damage.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.23, Ladders (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A portable ladder has to be set up in a doorway where foot traffic could knock it over. What does 1910.23(c)(7) require?

options.A: The ladder is secured to prevent accidental displacement, or guarded by a temporary barricade such as traffic cones or caution tape
options.B: A sign is hung on the ladder, with no other measure
options.C: The ladder is used only for tasks that take less than 15 minutes
options.D: The employee on the ladder calls out a warning before each move

questions.explanation: Ladders placed in passageways, doorways, or driveways where they can be displaced by other activities or traffic must be "secured to prevent accidental displacement" or "guarded by a temporary barricade, such as a row of traffic cones or caution tape, to keep the activities or traffic away from the ladder."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.23, Ladders (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: When does 1910.23(c)(12) allow ladders or ladder sections to be tied or fastened together to provide added length?

options.A: Whenever the joint is lashed with rope at two points
options.B: Whenever the combined ladder is less than 30 feet long
options.C: Whenever a supervisor approves the setup
options.D: Only when they are specifically designed for such use

questions.explanation: The employer must ensure "Ladders and ladder sections are not tied or fastened together to provide added length unless they are specifically designed for such use."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.23, Ladders (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under 1910.25(b)(7), what is the smallest tank or round-structure diameter at which winding stairways may be used on it?

options.A: 3 feet
options.B: 5 feet (1.5 m)
options.C: 8 feet
options.D: 12 feet

questions.explanation: Standard stairs are the rule for regular travel between levels, but "Winding stairways may be used on tanks and similar round structures when the diameter of the tank or structure is at least 5 feet (1.5 m)."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.25, Stairways (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: When may an employer use spiral, ship, or alternating tread-type stairs instead of standard stairs?

options.A: Only when the employer can demonstrate that it is not feasible to provide standard stairs
options.B: Whenever they cost less than standard stairs
options.C: Whenever fewer than 10 employees use the stairs
options.D: Whenever the employer prefers them, with no conditions

questions.explanation: "Spiral, ship, or alternating tread-type stairs are used only when the employer can demonstrate that it is not feasible to provide standard stairs."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.25, Stairways (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: What load does 1910.25(b)(6) require each stair to be able to support?

options.A: The normal anticipated live load, with no safety factor and no minimum concentrated load
options.B: A load of 200 pounds applied at the handrail, with no requirement for the treads
options.C: Four times the maximum intended load, with no minimum concentrated load
options.D: At least five times the normal anticipated live load, but never less than a concentrated load of 1,000 pounds applied at any point

questions.explanation: The employer must ensure "Each stair can support at least five times the normal anticipated live load, but never less than a concentrated load of 1,000 pounds (454 kg) applied at any point."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.25, Stairways (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: What does 1910.26(e) require portable dockboards to be equipped with?

options.A: Built-in warning lights
options.B: Wheels at every corner
options.C: Handholds or other means to permit safe handling
options.D: A hydraulic lifting mechanism

questions.explanation: The employer must ensure "Portable dockboards are equipped with handholds or other means to permit safe handling of dockboards."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.26, Dockboards (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A dockboard is used solely for materials handling with motorized equipment, and the employees are trained under 1910.30. Guardrails or handrails are then not required if the employees are not exposed to fall hazards greater than how many feet?

options.A: 15 feet
options.B: 10 feet
options.C: 20 feet
options.D: 30 feet

questions.explanation: A guardrail system or handrails are not required when dockboards are used solely for materials handling with motorized equipment, "employees engaged in these operations are not exposed to fall hazards greater than 10 feet (3 m)," and they are trained under 1910.30.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.28, Duty to have fall protection and falling object protection (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A service pit less than 10 feet deep uses the 1910.28(b)(8) option instead of a fall protection system. What must the readily visible caution signs posted at the pit state?

options.A: Danger—Keep Out
options.B: Caution—Open Pit
options.C: Watch Your Step
options.D: Authorized Personnel Only

questions.explanation: Among the conditions for not using a fall protection system at such a pit, the employer "Posts readily visible caution signs that meet the requirements of § 1910.145 and state “Caution—Open Pit.”"

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.28, Duty to have fall protection and falling object protection (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Section 1910.28(a)(2) lists situations to which the section does not apply. Which one is on that list?

options.A: Fixed ladders that extend more than 24 feet above a lower level
options.B: Hoist areas
options.C: Runways and similar walkways
options.D: Portable ladders

questions.explanation: 1910.28(a)(2) states that the section does not apply "to portable ladders." Fixed ladders, hoist areas, and runways each have their own fall protection paragraphs in 1910.28(b).

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.28, Duty to have fall protection and falling object protection (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Part of the cage on a fixed ladder that extends more than 24 feet above a lower level is replaced. Under 1910.28(b)(9)(i)(C), what must be installed?

options.A: A personal fall arrest system or ladder safety system in at least the section where the replacement is located
options.B: A new cage on that section, with nothing else
options.C: A warning sign at the base of the ladder, with nothing else
options.D: Nothing, as long as the replacement cage matches the original

questions.explanation: When "a fixed ladder, cage, or well, or any portion of a section thereof, is replaced, a personal fall arrest system or ladder safety system is installed in at least that section of the fixed ladder, cage, or well where the replacement is located."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.28, Duty to have fall protection and falling object protection (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: By what date does 1910.28(b)(9)(i)(D) require all fixed ladders that extend more than 24 feet above a lower level to be equipped with a personal fall arrest system or a ladder safety system?

options.A: November 18, 2040
options.B: January 1, 2046
options.C: November 18, 2036
options.D: November 19, 2050

questions.explanation: Under the final deadline for fixed ladders that extend more than 24 feet above a lower level, "on and after November 18, 2036, all fixed ladders are equipped with a personal fall arrest system or a ladder safety system."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.28, Duty to have fall protection and falling object protection (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: When a guardrail system uses intermediate vertical members such as balusters, what is the farthest apart 1910.29(b)(2)(iii) allows them to be installed?

options.A: 21 inches
options.B: 24 inches
options.C: 30 inches
options.D: 19 inches (48 cm)

questions.explanation: Where there is no wall or parapet at least 21 inches high, "Intermediate vertical members (such as balusters) are installed no more than 19 inches (48 cm) apart."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.29, Fall protection systems and falling object protection—criteria and practices (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Which material does 1910.29(b)(8) bar from use as top rails or midrails of a guardrail system?

options.A: Steel banding and plastic banding
options.B: Manila or synthetic rope
options.C: Wood
options.D: Steel pipe

questions.explanation: The rule says "Steel banding and plastic banding are not used for top rails or midrails." Manila or synthetic rope may be used if it is inspected as necessary to keep meeting the strength requirements.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.29, Fall protection systems and falling object protection—criteria and practices (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under 1910.30(b)(2), what must the employer train each employee who uses a dockboard to do?

options.A: Calculate the dockboard's rated load from its dimensions
options.B: Properly place and secure it to prevent unintentional movement
options.C: Weld cracks in the dockboard surface
options.D: Drive the transport vehicle into position at the dock

questions.explanation: The rule says "The employer must train each employee who uses a dockboard to properly place and secure it to prevent unintentional movement."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.30, Training requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Which situation does 1910.30(c) list as one requiring retraining?

options.A: A new calendar year begins, with no change in work or equipment
options.B: The employee moves to a different shift with the same hazards and equipment
options.C: Changes in the workplace render previous training obsolete or inadequate
options.D: The employer changes its payroll provider

questions.explanation: Retraining is required when the employer has reason to believe the employee lacks the required understanding and skill, including "when changes in the workplace render previous training obsolete or inadequate."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.30, Training requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)
